newsitem.title: NORWAY: NORDIC SKIING-RUSSIA APOLOGISE BEFORE WINNING RELAY GOLD.
newsitem.headline: NORDIC SKIING-RUSSIA APOLOGISE BEFORE WINNING RELAY GOLD.

text.p: After apologising to the public for the disqualification of Lyubov Yegorova for doping, Yelena Vialbe helped Russia cruise to victory in Thursday's 4x5-km women's relay at the Nordic skiing world championships.
Before the start of the race, Vialbe took a microphone and addressed the crowd, saying Russia felt sorry for what had happened but were not responsible as a team.

"The whole team want to apologise to the public and the king (King Harald of Norway) for what happened but you must understand that Lyubov Yegorova acted indiviually and that the team is not to blame," she said.
Yegorova was excluded from the championships on Wednesday and stripped of the gold medal she had won in Sunday's 5-km after testing positive for the banned stimulant Bromantan.

Even without her, world and Olympic champions Russia were in a class of their own in the relay with Olga Danilova, Larissa Lasutina, Nina Gavrilyuk and Vialbe clocking a winning time of 56 minutes 40.20 seconds.
The home team, whose four competitors had Norwegian flags painted on their cheeks, made the best start amid roars from a delighted 20,000 crowd.

But with seven km remaining, Gavrilyuk overtook Norwegian Elin Nilsen to give Russia the lead before allowing Vialbe to start the final lap some 10 seconds ahead of Norway's last skier, Trude Dybendahl-Hartz .
"I know how good Yelena is and I did try my best to catch her but it was impossible," said Trude Dybendhal, who crossed the line 16 seconds after Vialbe to hand Norway the silver medal.
There was a close battle for third place between Finland and Italy which Finland won when Satu Salonen outsprinted Manuela di Centa in the finishing straight.
When she realised that she would not be caught, Vialbe picked up a Russian flag from the crowd and waved it until the line.
The Russian win means Vialbe has now won four golds in as many women's cross-country events held so far in the championships.
Vialbe, who won the 15-km freestyle and the 10-km pursuit, was awarded gold for Sunday's 5-km race, in which she came second, after Yegorova was disqualified.
